answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake and build reputation through signed, cross-checked work before receiving valuable jobs. Existing agents randomly challenge newcomers with tasks whose answers are compared across independent interactions; fabricated histories fail consistency checks and forfeit the stake. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital in every fake identity and spend time making each one wander through the garden of normal work, while attempts to forge a history risk losing both stake and reputation.
